title: Performance Inspector: Unified Route & Model Timeline + Token Waterfall Charts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a design spec and interactive prototype for a consolidated "Performance Inspector" dashboard that surfaces per-model and per-route performance trends (latency, throughput, token metrics, cost correlation) and a token-waterfall visualization for tracing single-request behavior. This ticket captures visual layout, chart primitives, data aggregation rules, filtering UX, and accessibility considerations.

Scope (this ticket):
- High-fidelity prototype for the dashboard landing and detail flows (model-level, route-level).
- Chart specs for: timeline charts (latency p50/p95/p99), throughput (requests/sec & concurrency heatmap), token-rate and token-cost correlation, and Token Waterfall (per-request token timeline).
- Interaction patterns: time-range zoom, compare-by (model vs route), percentile toggles, overlay SLO thresholds, and drill-down to individual traces.
- Export/Share and Embed behaviors for dashboards (link + snapshot).
- Accessibility: color contrast, keyboard nav for chart tooltips, aria labels for interactive controls.

Out of scope: backend instrumentation changes, alerting rules implementation, autoscaling controls (covered in ENG-3421).

Notes: Prototype aims to balance observability needs of platform engineers and product owners. Emphasis on quick pattern recognition (percentile bands + anomaly markers) and a compact Token Waterfall to illustrate prompt vs KV/prefix reuse vs generated tokens and where latency originates.
decisions: Use a single unified timeline view that can toggle scope (model / route / project) instead of separate pages — reduces navigation overhead.
Show latency as an area representing 50/95/99 percentiles with median line; users can add a moving-average smoothing toggle.
Token Waterfall will be a compact horizontal swimlane per request with segments: prefix, cached-kv, generation, post-processing; color-coded and annotated with token counts and millisecond durations.
Default time window: last 6 hours with quick presets (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d). Custom ranges preserved in shared links.
For large date ranges (>7d) downsample points using max/min + p95 sampling per aggregation bucket to preserve tail behavior.
Percentile computation strategy: client displays p50/p95/p99 computed on pre-aggregated histograms from the backend (ENG-3421). Frontend will not recompute raw histograms.
SLO overlay: allow pinned thresholds per model/route; thresholds shown as dashed horizontal lines with traffic-weighted violation badges.
Accessibility: use colorblind-friendly palette and redundant encodings (pattern + color) for percentile bands.
Charts use consistent color tokens across the console: latency = blue, throughput = teal, tokens = purple, cost = amber.
chart_spec_summary: Timeline - Latency Bands: Type=Area+Line; X=time; Y=ms; Series=median(line), p50/p95/p99(area bands); Aggregation=histogram buckets aggregated per bucket interval; Render up to 10k points with downsampling beyond 1h intervals.
Throughput Overview: Type=Line+Bar; X=time; Left Y=req/sec (line); Right Y=concurrency (bar/heat); Series=total reqs, successful reqs, errors (stacked); Aggregation=sum per interval.

Token Rate & Cost Correlation: Type=Scatter+Line; X=tokens/sec or tokens/request; Y=cost-per-token (or estimated cost per request); Points show sample density; Trendline uses robust regression to highlight cost anomalies.

Token Waterfall (per-request): Type=Segmented Horizontal Bar; Segments=prefix(KV reuse), KV-fetch, decode/generation, post-process; Labels=token-count (n) + duration(ms); Hover shows full trace and links to raw trace in Tracing UI.
Concurrency Heatmap: Type=Heatmap; X=time buckets; Y=concurrency buckets; Cell intensity=request count; Useful to surface burst patterns and autoscaler interaction windows.
Anomaly Markers: Type=Event overlay; Display: vertical markers with tooltip summarizing spike cause (deployments, config changes, model swap).
aggregation_rules: Default interval selection: auto based on time range (1m for <=1h, 5m for <=24h, 1h for <=7d, 6h for >7d).
When computing percentile bands for large ranges, retrieve histogram quantiles from backend; frontend composes p50/p95/p99 for display.
Token-waterfall samples: show up to 20 recent request waterfalls by default for a selected time window; allow sampling strategy selection: latest, slowest, highest-cost, custom filter.
Downsampling policy: preserve max and p95 values per aggregation bucket to avoid masking tail spikes when reducing points.
Cost estimation: use standardized cost-per-token mapping based on model variant; for multi-model routes, weight cost by model invocation share.
interaction_patterns: Hover tooltip: shows aggregated metrics for the point (median, p95, p99, sample count, error rate).
Click-to-drill: clicking a timeline point opens a side panel with top N slow requests and Token Waterfalls.
Compare-by control: split timeline into overlay or stacked mode when comparing model vs route or environment (prod/staging).
SLO pin: user can pin/unpin an SLO threshold to all timelines; pinned SLOs appear across views and can be exported with snapshot links.
Annotate: allow adding a short note tied to a timestamp (deployment, config change); annotations show on all relevant charts.
Keyboard navigation: left/right arrows move time window by step; focusable legend items toggle series visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype available in Figma demonstrating default landing view, drill-down, Token Waterfall, and compare-by interactions.
Chart spec document accepted by Eng (ENG-3421) and PM (PM-412) covering aggregation rules and downsampling.
Design review feedback items addressed (contrast, tooltip verbosity, mobile breakpoint) and sign-off recorded.
A11y checks: contrast ratios and keyboard navigation verified in lightweight audit.
Handoff package uploaded to Drive with tokens, color variables, and exportable assets.
user_research_notes: 2026-02-26 - Internal session with 4 SREs/Platform Engineers: primary ask was quicker identification of tail latency causes; Token Waterfall was unanimously considered useful for root-cause reasoning.
2026-03-02 - PM-led review with three product owners: they favored the unified timeline and asked for a compact exportable snapshot for stakeholder reports.
Key insight: users want both high-level trends (6h/24h) and an easy path to see the slowest 5 requests with full token breakdown. Sampling UI must not be hidden.
